transcription: Fact-sheet text only, from the HTML edition served at the locator (https://pubs.usgs.gov/fs/fs002-97/ itself now serves a directory index listing fs00297.pdf, images/ and 'old html files/'; the page's own footer still names that URL). The page has no H1: the title line is its displayed title ('What Are Volcano Hazards?'). Removed: the USGS banner image and masthead ('U.S. Geological Survey / Fact Sheet 002-97 / Revised March 2008 / Superceded by Fact Sheet 2018-3075'), the author and graphics credits (kept in the attribution field), the contact address, the Cascades Volcano Observatory link, the cooperating-organizations list, related fact sheets, the PDF and Spanish-edition links, the closing slogan and the URL/maintainer footer. Kept: the boxed introduction, the opening paragraph, the hazard-diagram caption as its own line (the diagram is stored separately as figure usgs-volcano-hazards-1), the section headings as their own lines, and the Mount Shasta photo/map caption as its own line (photo and map not stored). Bold hazard terms flattened to plain text (the page bolds only 'round water' of 'ground water'; rendered as 'ground water'); SiO<sub>2</sub> flattened to SiO2; °F as °F. The page serves four U+FFFD replacement characters where apostrophes belong (Earth’s twice, lava’s, volcano’s); each is rendered as ’. Page quirks kept as printed: the Volcanic Gases paragraph that ends mid-sentence ('… by altering chlorine and nitrogen' with no ending), and the dated 'During the past 15 years' wording. Whitespace normalised, LF.
purpose: library: the hazards of a typical Cascade/Alaska stratovolcano — eruption columns and clouds (tephra, bombs within 2 miles of the vent, ash rising more than 12 miles in under 30 minutes, ash fall over 22,000 square miles from Mount St. Helens, the aviation hazard), volcanic gases (fumaroles and cracks; >90% water vapor from heated ground water; sulfur dioxide and acid rain; carbon dioxide pooling; fluorine), lava flows and domes (silica content: low-silica basalt fast and fluid, andesite/dacite thick and sluggish, dacite and rhyolite lava domes), pyroclastic flows (up to 1,500°F, 100–150 mph, surges and the 1980 lateral blast), volcano landslides (debris avalanches, the Mount Shasta / Weed example) and lahars (20–40 mph, more than 50 miles), plus USGS monitoring. Carries figure usgs-volcano-hazards-1 (Bobbie Myers' labelled volcano hazards diagram with a silica/magma-type scale) for label the diagram; also fits sort-into-groups (eruption vs non-eruption hazards), a compare table of hazards (speed, reach) and quiz cards with predict-then-reveal. Note: superseded by USGS Fact Sheet 2018-3075 ('Living With Volcano Hazards'); some counts are dated (2008 revision).
